subject.title: [Bug]: Scheduled isolated agentTurn outer run records error although session ended success

question: For successful isolated cron execution followed by completion-delivery failure, should the persisted parent run status remain `ok` with delivery-specific failure fields, or should OpenClaw add a first-class partial-success/warning status?
rationale: Both options are represented by open PRs and affect operator tooling, backoff, failure alerts, Gateway/API consumers, and UI semantics; automation should not choose that product contract unilaterally.

options.title: Accept narrow `ok` plus delivery fields
options.body: Land the proof-sufficient narrow candidate so execution success remains `ok` while `deliveryStatus` and `deliveryError` carry the failed delivery phase.

options.title: Choose first-class warning status
options.body: Keep the narrow PR paused and route the behavior through the broader warning-status contract across storage, Gateway, CLI, UI, plugins, and docs.

options.title: Wait for live repro before choosing
options.body: Keep both implementation paths paused until a maintainer gets a live scheduled provider/channel reproduction of the original WSL2 service path.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow `ok` plus delivery fields
recommendation.body: Land the proof-sufficient narrow candidate so execution success remains `ok` while `deliveryStatus` and `deliveryError` carry the failed delivery phase.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron status/finalization history and release ownership make this the best available routing candidate for the semantics choice.
